description: Multivariate Electrical Measurements of Household Appliances with Synchronized Zone Occupancy Tracking is a data set described in a peer-reviewed Scientific Data article written by Vaclav Kolar et al. Home energy management systems can reduce electricity consumption and operating costs, leading to environmental benefits. Their effective operation relies on accurate information about real-time and long-term appliance usage, which can be obtained via nonintrusive load monitoring (NILM). Progress in NILM, including fair benchmarking of algorithms, critically depends on well-documented, high-quality datasets. Coverage: a single site or case study; published in 2026. The formats are not stated in the sources read. The paper's page was read, but no repository address could be taken from its machine-readable metadata, so the record links to the article, whose Data Records section names where the data sit. Access is free of charge and open according to the article. The licence of the data is not stated in the sources read (the paper itself is open access). Caveats: written from the Scientific Data article metadata (title, abstract, Data Records section) read on 2026-10-01; the data themselves were not opened or downloaded, so their contents, quality and current availability were not checked. It can support power-system, energy-planning and grid-operation studies. Related records: none catalogued yet.
